concepts.name: Origins and Evolution: From Shanghai Five to SCO
key_dimensions: Shanghai Five (1996) founding members: Russia, China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan — NOT Uzbekistan initially
Transformation to SCO in 2001 with inclusion of Uzbekistan — the exact trigger and year
Original mandate was border demilitarization and confidence-building, NOT economic integration — evolution of purpose
Distinction between Shanghai Five's security focus vs. SCO's broader economic-security-cultural mandate

concepts.name: SCO Membership: Full Members, Observers, and Dialogue Partners
key_dimensions: Current full members (9 as of 2023): China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran — Iran's full membership in 2023 is a frequent trap
Observer States vs. Dialogue Partners — distinction in rights, obligations, and participation levels
Belarus accession process — status as of 2024 (approved for full membership at Astana Summit 2023)
UPSC trap: Confusing Afghanistan's status (observer) with full membership, and Turkey/Saudi Arabia as dialogue partners

concepts.name: India's Accession to SCO: Timeline, Conditions, and Strategic Calculus
key_dimensions: India became full member in 2017 at Astana Summit — along with Pakistan simultaneously (critical trap point)
India had Observer status since 2005 — 12-year gap before full membership
Strategic rationale: Central Asian connectivity, energy security, counter-terrorism vs. concerns about China-Pakistan axis within SCO
India's selective engagement — signing some SCO agreements while abstaining on BRI-linked initiatives within SCO framework

concepts.name: SCO Organizational Structure: Principal Bodies and Decision-Making
key_dimensions: Council of Heads of State — supreme decision-making body, meets annually
Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) — focuses on trade/economic cooperation, separate from Heads of State council
SCO Secretariat (Beijing) vs. RATS Executive Committee (Tashkent) — two permanent bodies with distinct mandates
Consensus-based decision-making — no voting mechanism, implication for India blocking China-Pakistan joint proposals

concepts.name: RATS: Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure — Mandate and Significance
key_dimensions: Headquartered in Tashkent, Uzbekistan — distinguish from SCO Secretariat in Beijing
Three Evils doctrine: terrorism, separatism, extremism — UPSC frequently tests the exact three evils
RATS coordinates intelligence sharing and joint counter-terrorism exercises — operational vs. strategic role
India's engagement with RATS and tensions given Pakistan's simultaneous membership — inherent structural contradiction

concepts.name: SCO vs. Other Regional Groupings: Overlaps and Distinctions
key_dimensions: SCO vs. CSTO (Collective Security Treaty Organization) — membership overlap but different mandates; CSTO is a military alliance, SCO is not
SCO vs. ASEAN — SCO lacks a formal free trade agreement unlike ASEAN's AFTA; comparison of institutional depth
SCO vs. BRICS — overlapping membership (India, China, Russia) but SCO is geographically Eurasian while BRICS is global; different economic focus
SCO vs. ECO (Economic Cooperation Organization) — Central Asian overlap, Iran and Pakistan in both

concepts.name: SCO's Economic Agenda: Trade, Connectivity, and the BRI Tension
key_dimensions: SCO does NOT have a common currency or free trade agreement — a key limitation vs. EU/ASEAN
SCO Business Council and SCO Interbank Consortium — two economic facilitation bodies, not full institutions
China's push to use SCO as a vehicle for BRI promotion vs. India's resistance — institutional battleground
SCO Development Bank proposal — repeatedly discussed but not established, unlike BRICS's NDB

concepts.name: SCO and Central Asian Energy Security
key_dimensions: Central Asian members (Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan indirectly, Uzbekistan) hold significant hydrocarbon reserves — SCO as energy corridor framework
India's interest in TAPI (Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India) pipeline within the SCO connectivity context
Competition between Russian and Chinese energy influence within SCO framework — structural tension
Iran's full membership (2023) adding critical energy dimension — Persian Gulf to Central Asia connectivity

concepts.name: SCO Summits: Key Decisions and Locations (Examinable Milestones)
key_dimensions: 2001 Shanghai Summit — formal establishment of SCO and SCO Charter signed
2017 Astana Summit — India and Pakistan's full membership; landmark expansion
2022 Samarkand Summit — first in-person post-COVID, Iran observer-to-member process initiated, discussions on de-dollarization
2023 New Delhi Summit (India's chairmanship) — held virtually, SCO Development Bank discussed, India's 'One Earth, One Family, One Future' theme; Belarus approved

concepts.name: India's Chairmanship of SCO (2022-23): Agenda and Outcomes
key_dimensions: India's five priority areas: startups/innovation, traditional medicine, digital inclusion, youth empowerment, shared Buddhist heritage — distinctly soft-power focus
First SCO Summit held in virtual format under India's chairmanship (June 2023) — procedural significance
India promoted SCO as platform for 'SECURE' framework (Security, Economy, Connectivity, Unity, Respect for sovereignty, Environment) — Modi's coinage
India's push for trade in local currencies within SCO — aligns with de-dollarization theme but also India's rupee trade ambitions

concepts.name: SCO and Afghanistan: The Elephant in the Room
key_dimensions: Afghanistan has Observer status — Taliban government's recognition not endorsed by SCO collectively
SCO-Afghanistan Contact Group — mechanism for engagement, predates Taliban takeover
Divergent SCO member positions on Taliban recognition: China/Russia more pragmatic vs. India's cautious approach
Afghanistan's territory as critical missing link in SCO's connectivity vision — INSTC and other corridors

concepts.name: SCO and De-dollarization: Trade in Local Currencies
key_dimensions: SCO platform increasingly used to discuss reducing USD dependence in intra-SCO trade
China's yuan promotion within SCO vs. Russia's ruble push post-2022 sanctions — competing currency interests
India's position: promoting rupee settlements but cautious about yuan dominance within SCO trade
No formal SCO mechanism for currency settlement exists yet — aspirational vs. operational distinction

concepts.name: Pakistan-India Dynamics within SCO: Structural Tensions
key_dimensions: Both admitted simultaneously in 2017 — China's strategic motive in ensuring Pakistan's entry alongside India
Consensus rule means India cannot be outvoted but also cannot isolate Pakistan within SCO
SCO as platform where India-Pakistan foreign ministers meet on sidelines — Track 1.5 diplomacy potential
CPEC (China-Pakistan Economic Corridor) runs through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir — India's sovereignty objection creates BRI-SCO nexus tension

concepts.name: SCO's Security Architecture: Military Exercises and Peace Mission
key_dimensions: 'Peace Mission' series — joint counter-terrorism military exercises conducted under SCO, not RATS
SCO is NOT a military alliance (no Article 5-type collective defense) — critical distinction from NATO/CSTO
India's participation in Peace Mission exercises — engagement despite India-China border tensions
Frequency and rotating host responsibility for Peace Mission — demonstrates operational security cooperation

concepts.name: SCO's Cultural and People-to-People Dimension
key_dimensions: SCO Forum — civil society engagement platform
SCO University network proposal and SCO Youth Council — soft power infrastructure
Shared Buddhist and Silk Road heritage as cultural diplomacy tool — India's leveraging of this within SCO
Traditional Medicine cooperation — India's push for Ayurveda/Yoga recognition within SCO framework (highlighted during India's chairmanship)

concepts.name: Iran's Full Membership (2023): Geopolitical Implications
key_dimensions: Iran was Observer since 2005 — 18-year gap before full membership; sanctions were the barrier
Iran's entry significantly expands SCO's geographic reach to Persian Gulf and Middle East
Strategic implication: SCO now encompasses major energy producers (Russia, Kazakhstan, Iran) — energy security dimension amplified
U.S. concern about SCO becoming an 'anti-Western' bloc intensified with Iran's entry — Western critique of SCO

concepts.name: SCO Secretariat: Functions, Location, and Secretary-General
key_dimensions: Located in Beijing — China's institutional influence through hosting the Secretariat
Secretary-General serves 3-year term, appointed by rotation among member states — not elected
Secretariat's administrative role vs. RATS's operational role — functional division of labor
SCO Secretariat budget contributions — proportional system, China's dominant contribution and its implications

concepts.name: SCO's Connectivity Agenda: INSTC, Corridors, and India's Engagement
key_dimensions: International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) — India-Iran-Russia route as India's alternative to BRI within SCO context
Chabahar Port (India-developed) as India's gateway to Central Asia bypassing Pakistan — SCO connectivity without BRI
SCO's lack of a dedicated connectivity fund vs. China's BRI financing — institutional gap
Afghanistan as missing link: SCO connectivity vision requires stable Afghanistan; Taliban complicates this

concepts.name: SCO and Multilateralism: Positioning vis-à-vis UN and Western Institutions
key_dimensions: SCO explicitly endorses UN Charter principles and multilateralism — but critics see it as challenging Western-led order
SCO's non-interference principle vs. R2P (Responsibility to Protect) — divergence from Western liberal international order
SCO-UN cooperation agreement exists — SCO has observer status at UN General Assembly
Perception gap: SCO members position it as inclusive multilateralism; Western view is it as a counter-NATO/counter-G7 formation

concepts.name: SCO's Limitations and Criticisms: Why It Underperforms Its Potential
key_dimensions: No free trade agreement despite 20+ years — economic integration far behind ASEAN or EU
China-India rivalry paralyzes consensus on connectivity (BRI) and security matters
Russia-China competition for regional leadership within SCO — two 800-pound gorillas problem
Expansion paradox: Adding India, Pakistan, Iran increased geopolitical weight but also internal contradictions — enlargement vs. effectiveness tradeoff
